name: STARTER_ctrl_1
title: Starter Control
description: Controls the starter sequence of the turbine.

description.purpose: The air inlet housing in the turbine starter directs compressed air from the aircraft’s pneumatic supply or APU into the turbine section of the ATS. Its purpose is to ensure smooth airflow distribution for efficient turbine rotation during engine start.
description.Location: The air inlet housing is located at the entry point of the Air Turbine Starter (ATS), connecting the pneumatic supply line to the turbine assembly.
description.Description: The air inlet housing is a robust, precision-cast component designed to withstand high-pressure compressed air. It typically includes an air inlet flange, internal flow passages, and seals to prevent leakage. The housing may also integrate ports for mounting the Starter Air Valve (SAV) and provisions for directing airflow uniformly onto the turbine blades.
description.Operation: During engine start, compressed air enters the ATS through the air inlet housing. The housing guides the airflow and delivers it at the proper angle and pressure to the turbine wheel, causing it to rotate. This rotational energy is transmitted through the reduction gears and output shaft to crank the engine. The housing must remain free from leaks, cracks, or blockages to ensure efficient starting performance.

description.purpose: The magnetic plug assembly in the turbine starter is designed to attract and capture ferrous particles from the lubricating oil. This helps in monitoring internal wear of gears, bearings, and other rotating components, ensuring early detection of potential damage.
description.Location: The magnetic plug assembly is installed on the ATS housing, usually at a low point in the lubrication system where oil circulation ensures contact with the plug. Its placement allows easy inspection and cleaning during routine maintenance.
description.Description: The magnetic plug assembly consists of a threaded plug embedded with a permanent magnet. The magnet attracts and holds fine metal particles suspended in the lubricating oil, preventing them from circulating further and causing additional wear. The plug is removable, allowing technicians to visually inspect and clean collected debris during scheduled servicing.
description.Operation: During operation, as lubricating oil circulates through the ATS, the magnetic plug continuously captures metallic debris produced by normal component wear or early-stage damage. Collected debris provides maintenance personnel with a diagnostic indicator of internal health. Regular inspection of the magnetic plug is essential to detect abnormal wear conditions, prevent severe damage, and ensure reliable operation of the turbine starter.

description.purpose: The output shaft in the turbine starter transmits the mechanical power generated by the air turbine to the engine accessory gearbox. This enables the engine’s core to rotate during start-up, providing the necessary momentum for ignition and acceleration.
description.Location: The output shaft is located at the forward end of the Air Turbine Starter (ATS), connecting the internal reduction gear assembly of the starter to the engine accessory gearbox drive pad.
description.Description: The output shaft is a precision-machined, high-strength steel shaft designed to handle high torque and rotational loads. It is supported by lubricated bearings and connected through splines or couplings to ensure secure torque transfer. The shaft is protected against misalignment and designed to withstand repeated start cycles without excessive wear.
description.Operation: During operation, the compressed air drives the turbine and gear assembly inside the ATS. This rotational energy is transmitted through the output shaft to the engine accessory gearbox. As the shaft turns, it spins the engine’s compressor section, enabling airflow for combustion and eventual self-sustaining engine operation. Proper lubrication of the bearings supporting the shaft is essential to minimize friction, prevent overheating, and ensure long service life.

description.purpose: The starter speed sensor is designed to detect the speed of the Air Turbine Starter (ATS). It transmits this data to both the Electronic Engine Control (EEC) and the Power and Health Monitoring Unit (PHMU) for failure analysis.
description.Location: This sensor is mounted on the ATS housing at the 3:00 position.
description.Description: The starter speed sensor is a one-piece, hermetically sealed unit. It consists of a dual-channel magnetic speed sensor that uses a single permanent magnet, two separate coils, and one electrical connector. The speed signal generated by the sensor is first sent to the EEC and then to the PHMU. This signal helps in detecting potential failure conditions, which may include: 1. Starter Air Valve (SAV) failure in the open position during start. 2. Uncommanded opening of the SAV after start. 3. Shearing of the starter drive shaft.
description.Operation: The starter speed sensor functions by detecting the rotational speed of the starter ring gear. As the teeth of the ring gear pass the tip of the magnetic probe, they cause variations in the magnetic field. These changes generate a time-varying electrical pulse signal. This signal is then processed by the EEC and PHMU, where it is converted into a calculated rotational speed. This processed information enables the monitoring systems to ensure proper operation and identify any abnormal conditions.

description.purpose: The oil fill in the turbine starter is provided to lubricate the internal rotating components of the Air Turbine Starter (ATS), such as bearings and gears. Proper lubrication reduces friction, prevents wear, and ensures smooth and reliable operation during engine starting cycles.
description.Location: The oil fill port is located on the ATS housing, typically marked with a cap or plug for easy access during maintenance. Its placement allows convenient refilling and inspection of oil levels.
description.Description: The oil fill is a dedicated port designed for adding and maintaining the correct level of lubricating oil in the ATS. It usually consists of a threaded or sealed opening, equipped with an oil filler cap to prevent leakage and contamination. The oil used is a specialized lubricating fluid compatible with turbine starter systems. Adequate oil supply inside the ATS ensures that the bearings, reduction gears, and shaft assemblies operate under optimal conditions, minimizing overheating and component damage.
description.Operation: During operation, the lubricating oil distributed through the internal passages of the ATS forms a thin film between moving parts, reducing direct metal-to-metal contact. This lubrication process ensures efficient torque transmission from the air turbine to the engine accessory gearbox. Regular oil checks and refills through the oil fill port are essential to maintain ATS health. Low oil levels or contamination can lead to increased friction, overheating, gear wear, or even complete starter failure.
